subject.title: fix(groq): keep default Llama agent turns within TPM limit

question: Should the default Groq fix preserve tools automatically for users with an explicit request budget, or intentionally require a separate `compat.supportsTools: true` migration step?
rationale: The current branch fixes the base-tier failure by changing an existing model capability default for every user, and repository policy treats that upgrade/operator impact as a maintainer-owned compatibility choice.

options.title: Preserve configured tool use
options.body: Make the chat-only fallback conditional on the absence of an explicit max-token budget, so higher-tier and already-configured users retain tools without a new compatibility override.

options.title: Accept the global tool default
options.body: Merge the model-wide tool opt-out and explicitly own the upgrade behavior, documentation, and proof that existing users can restore tools with configuration.

options.title: Pause for a tier-aware design
options.body: Hold the PR until the provider can select a safe tool budget from known Groq tier metadata or another reliable runtime signal.

recommendation.title: Preserve configured tool use
recommendation.body: Make the chat-only fallback conditional on the absence of an explicit max-token budget, so higher-tier and already-configured users retain tools without a new compatibility override.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the current Groq catalog/default model path and is best positioned to decide the bundled provider's upgrade policy.
